items.question: What row order does the CSV use?
items.chose: Sorts rows by creation time ascending, then by id ascending, on a copy of the input.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What does the CSV contain when the requisition list is empty?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header line only.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or the header without a BOM.

items.question: Does the CSV start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.chose: Prefixes the output with a BOM (U+FEFF).

items.question: Which line terminator does the CSV use?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Use LF, and leave off the final newline.

items.question: What are the column names and their order?
items.instead: Use snake_case or field-name headers (id,title,status,openings,filled,createdAt), or add other columns such as a remaining count.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the full UTC ISO 8601 string with milliseconds.
items.instead: Write a date only (YYYY-MM-DD) or a locale-formatted date.

items.question: How is a null or undefined title written?
items.instead: Write the text 'null' or 'undefined', or reject the requisition.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Quotes the field per RFC 4180 and doubles any embedded quotes.
items.instead: Do the same and also quote or neutralise fields starting with =, +, -, @ to block spreadsheet formula injection.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unrecognised status?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id, and only four statuses are accepted: open, on_hold, filled, cancelled.
items.instead: Pass the status through unchanged, or skip the row.

items.question: What counts as a valid openings or filled count?
items.chose: Accepts only safe integers of 0 or more, and throws for negative, fractional, NaN, infinite or unsafe-large values.
items.instead: Accept any number, or clamp invalid values to 0.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id.
items.instead: Export the row as it is, or clamp filled to openings.

items.question: What happens when one requisition is invalid among valid ones?
items.chose: Validates every requisition before building anything, and one bad row makes the whole build throw.
items.instead: Skip the bad rows and export the rest, or collect all errors and report them together.
